The **Per-setting status** report goes further: for each setting in the policy, the number of devices in success, conflict or error, with the list of devices behind each number. It is the most effective tool for finding *which* setting makes a fifty-setting profile fail. The **Configuration policy assignment failures** report (Devices > Monitor) lists the policies that failed or are in conflict, with the device, the failing setting and sometimes an error code.
1essizt8s7j: ## Delay is part of the system
d9hbrbkp5e: Intune recalls three types of sync: **per change** (a notification prompts the device to sync when a policy is assigned, modified or deleted, or when a group changes), **client-initiated** (sign-in, state change) and **single device** (manual action). The notification delay varies from immediate to a few hours, and by platform (Google services on Android, busy conditions on iOS). A device that is off or offline receives the policy at its next sync. Reports can also lag behind the real state. Practical consequence: a "not evaluated" device is not a failing device, and a removed policy can remain assigned until the next sync, which is intended behavior.
bmnrhbz1y0: The **Troubleshooting + support > Troubleshoot** pane lets you pick a user and check at a glance the Intune license status, the **Managed** column (a device must be under MDM management, or EAS and MDM, to receive compliance and configuration policies), the Microsoft Entra join type and the compliance state. App protection policies, for their part, do not require device enrollment. Always start with this pane: half of the "policies that do not apply" come from a missing license or an unenrolled device.

omp7yrkn0q: ## Sync: the first response, not the only one
6l1oaw2v8: The **Sync** action forces a device to connect to Intune to receive pending actions and policies. It is offered on Android, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and Windows, with the Help Desk Operator role, Endpoint Security Manager or a custom role that contains the *Remote tasks/Sync devices* permission. On Windows, the sync covers policy processing, app detection, scripts and remediations; the device's **Sync status** tab exists only on Windows and iOS/iPadOS, with the new view preview enabled. A successful sync does not fix a poorly targeted policy: if the state stays "pending", go back to the targeting and the filters.
203rzkeclxj: The **Collect diagnostics** action (Windows) retrieves logs without interrupting the user: Intune management extension logs, Windows Update ETLs, the Defender report (`MpSupportFiles.cab`), join state (`dsregcmd /status`), firewall profiles, WinHTTP proxy, and more. Results are kept **28 days**, with at most **10 collections** per device, and the bulk action accepts **25 devices** at a time. It can also trigger automatically on a Windows Autopilot failure, once a day per device. Diagnostics cannot be collected or downloaded through a direct Graph call: you must go through the admin center. Privacy note: diagnostics may contain user or device names, and Microsoft staff may access them during a support incident. Treat them as sensitive data.
2f1cq30cfyg: ## Local logs and the MDM report
fbkz5uzo9b: When you have the device in hand, three sources dominate. The **MDM diagnostic report** (`MdmDiagnosticsTool`, or Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Export your management logs) gives the profiles received and their errors. The **DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider** event log (Admin) shows the delivery of each OMA-DM setting, as seen in module 13. The **Intune management extension** logs (`%ProgramData%\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs`) serve for scripts, Win32 applications and remediations. A symptom guides the choice: policy absent, look at the MDM report; application or script failing, look at the extension; update dragging, the Windows Update logs.
ov58ohjpql: A Windows device whose TPM module was factory reset loses its Microsoft Entra identity, because the identity is stored there. The sync fails with "0x80072f9a" and the only way out is **re-enrollment**. This kind of hardware cause appears in no profile report: hence the value of collection.

sx8vohulxp: ## The audit log: who changed what
10cgat85szn: The Intune audit log (**Tenant administration > Audit logs**) records the creations, modifications, assignments and deletions made in the service. Each event shows **the actor** (who, and through which application; an action made in the portal always lists the Intune portal extension) and the **targets** with the modified properties. It is exported to CSV, sent to Azure Monitor (storage, event hub or Log Analytics) to retain it and query it in KQL, and the Graph API gives **two years** of audit events. In an investigation: a policy was modified at 2 a.m.? The log says by whom. It does not say whether the change was legitimate, nor whether it was applied to the devices.
1ao2ta17gd: The Graph device management resources make it possible to read managed devices, profiles, compliance states and to run the sync action. Three rules of caution. **Read first**: reports and inventories through Graph avoid the click-by-click safely. **Least privilege**: grant read permissions to the application, not full management. **License required**: using Graph to configure Intune requires the service to be properly licensed. For diagnostics, Graph is not enough (lesson 2). Beta versions of the API can change: do not build production monitoring on a beta endpoint without noting it in the limits register.
eqjgam726z: A useful control combines a recurring report (noncompliant devices, assignment failures), the audit log routed to Log Analytics and an alert on changes to critical policies (firewall, compliance, Conditional Access). Keep few alerts but all actionable, with an owner. None of these building blocks replaces the periodic verification of samples on a device.
z75ehn2q1x: Microsoft's documentation changes often: deprecated templates (macOS, administrative templates), new supported versions (Linux), postponed deadlines (approved client apps). The program provides a **review procedure**: 1) read the source and its date; 2) identify the sheets, exercises and matrix cells affected; 3) correct the content, the nature of the coverage and the verification date; 4) rerun the content tests; 5) record the change in the change log and, if doubt remains, in the limits register. The rule: an assertion is never changed without changing its source and date.
